author: codex-authoring-run-2026-08-13-anatomy-01

why: Tapotement uses quick, light tapping or striking movements. It stimulates the area instead of using the slow gliding strokes of effleurage.
tapotement（叩击法）使用快速、轻柔的拍打动作，作用偏刺激，不同于 effleurage 的缓慢滑动。
refs: Manicuring - Massage Movements

why: The patella is the small bone in front of the knee joint. It protects the joint and helps the thigh muscles straighten the leg.
patella（髌骨）位于膝关节前方，保护关节，并帮助大腿肌肉伸直腿部。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Leg

why: The tibia is the large lower-leg bone commonly called the shinbone. It carries much of the body's weight between the knee and ankle.
tibia（胫骨）是小腿较大的骨，也叫 shinbone（胫骨），在膝与踝之间承受大部分体重。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Leg

why: The talus sits between the lower-leg bones and the heel bone. This large ankle bone transfers body weight into the foot.
talus（距骨）位于小腿骨与跟骨之间，把身体重量传到足部。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Foot

why: Abductor muscles move a body part away from the body's center line. In the hand, they spread the fingers apart.
abductor muscles（外展肌）让身体部位远离身体中线；在手部，它们使手指分开。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Hand

why: Abduction means movement away from the center. The hand's abductor muscles therefore move the fingers away from one another.
abduction 表示远离中线的动作，因此手部外展肌会让手指彼此分开。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Hand

why: The ulnar nerve travels along the little-finger side of the forearm and hand. It supplies feeling and movement to the little finger area.
ulnar nerve（尺神经）沿前臂和手的小指侧走行，负责小指区域的感觉和动作。
refs: General Anatomy - Nerves of the Arm and Hand

why: The humerus is the long bone between the shoulder and elbow. It forms the upper arm and connects with the forearm at the elbow.
humerus（肱骨）是肩与肘之间的长骨，构成上臂，并在肘部连接前臂。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Arm

why: Digital nerves are the small nerve branches that enter the fingers. They carry touch, pain, and temperature signals.
digital nerves（指神经）是进入手指的小神经分支，传递触觉、疼痛和温度信号。
lock: digital nerves = nerves of the fingers.
refs: General Anatomy - Nerves of the Hand

why: The five metacarpal bones form the palm between the wrist and fingers. Each one lines up with a finger or thumb.
五块 metacarpals（掌骨）在手腕与手指之间构成手掌，每一块对应一根手指或拇指。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Hand

why: Two small sesamoid bones usually sit under the joint at the base of the big toe. They help tendons move smoothly under pressure.
两块小的 sesamoid bones（籽骨）通常位于大脚趾根部关节下方，帮助肌腱在受压时顺畅移动。
lock: sesamoid bones = small bones under the big-toe joint.
籽骨 = 大脚趾关节下的小骨。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Foot

why: The tibia forms the front, weight-bearing part of the lower leg. Its common name is the shinbone.
tibia（胫骨）构成小腿前方主要承重部分，常用名称是 shinbone。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Leg

why: Shinbone is the everyday name for the tibia. It is the larger of the two lower-leg bones.
shinbone 是 tibia（胫骨）的日常名称，也是两块小腿骨中较大的一块。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Leg

why: Extensor muscles straighten a joint. Forearm extensors pull on tendons that open and straighten the fingers.
extensor muscles（伸肌）负责伸直关节。前臂伸肌牵拉肌腱，使手指张开并伸直。
lock: extensors straighten fingers; flexors bend them.
伸肌伸直手指；屈肌弯曲手指。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Forearm and Hand

why: Phalanges are the bones of the fingers and toes. Each finger has three, except the thumb, which has two.
phalanges（指骨或趾骨）构成手指和脚趾。每根手指有三块，拇指有两块。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Hand and Foot

why: The pronator muscle rotates the forearm so the palm turns downward or inward. The opposite action is turning the palm upward.
pronator muscle（旋前肌）使前臂旋转，让手掌向下或向内；相反动作是让手掌向上。
lock: pronator = palm turns inward or down.
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Forearm

why: Abductor muscles pull the fingers away from the hand's center. Adductor muscles perform the opposite action and bring them together.
abductor muscles（外展肌）使手指远离手部中线；adductor muscles 做相反动作，使手指合拢。
lock: 外展肌分开；内收肌合拢。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Hand

why: Histology studies tissues, which are groups of similar cells doing a shared job. Anatomy studies larger body structures.
histology（组织学）研究由相似细胞组成并共同工作的组织；anatomy 研究较大的身体结构。
refs: General Anatomy - Cells and Tissues

why: Slow, controlled massage can reduce muscle tension and calm the nervous system. This helps the client feel relaxed.
缓慢、稳定的按摩可减轻肌肉紧张并安抚神经系统，帮助客户感到放松。
lock: massage can reduce tension and support relaxation.
按摩可减轻紧张并帮助放松。
refs: Manicuring - Benefits of Massage

why: The calcaneus forms the heel and is the largest foot bone. The femur is larger, but it belongs to the thigh, not the foot.
calcaneus（跟骨）构成脚跟，是足部最大的骨。femur 更大，但它属于大腿，不属于足部。
lock: largest foot bone = calcaneus; largest thigh bone = femur.
足部最大骨 = 跟骨；大腿骨 = 股骨。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Foot

why: Tapotement is a series of fast tapping or striking movements. It is more stimulating than a slow gliding massage movement.
tapotement（叩击法）是一连串快速拍打动作，比缓慢滑动的按摩动作更有刺激性。
refs: Manicuring - Massage Movements

why: Nerve tissue receives signals and sends instructions between the brain, spinal cord, muscles, and organs. This communication coordinates body activity.
神经组织接收信号，并在大脑、脊髓、肌肉和器官之间传递指令，从而协调身体活动。
lock: 神经组织 = 接收、传递、协调。
refs: General Anatomy - Nerve Tissue

why: Adductor muscles move a body part toward the center line. In the hand, they bring separated fingers back together.
adductor muscles（内收肌）使身体部位靠近中线；在手部，它们把分开的手指合拢。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Hand

why: Gliding joints let flat bone surfaces slide over one another. The wrist and ankle use this small sliding movement for flexibility.
gliding joints（滑动关节）让较平的骨面彼此滑动。腕部和踝部利用这种小幅滑动获得灵活性。
lock: 腕部和踝部 = 滑动关节。
refs: General Anatomy - Joints

why: Metacarpals are five long, narrow bones that make the palm. They connect the wrist bones to the finger bones.
metacarpals（掌骨）是构成手掌的五块细长骨，连接腕骨和指骨。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Hand

why: Metatarsals are five long bones in the middle of the foot. They connect the ankle-area bones to the toe bones.
metatarsals（跖骨）是足部中间的五块长骨，连接踝部骨和趾骨。
refs: General Anatomy - Bones of the Foot

why: Growing cells take in nutrients and make waste. Removing that waste prevents harmful material from building up inside the cell.
生长中的细胞会吸收营养并产生废物。排出废物可防止有害物质在细胞内堆积。
lock: cell growth needs nutrients in and waste out.
细胞生长需要营养进入、废物排出。
refs: General Anatomy - Cell Functions

why: Metabolism includes all chemical activity that keeps cells alive. It changes nutrients into energy and materials the body can use.
metabolism（新陈代谢）包括维持细胞生命的全部化学活动，把营养转化为能量和身体可用的材料。
lock: metabolism = life-supporting chemical activity in cells.
metabolism = 细胞中维持生命的化学活动。
refs: General Anatomy - Metabolism

why: Massage pressure usually moves from a muscle's insertion toward its origin. This direction follows blood return toward the heart and avoids forcing blood outward.
按摩压力通常从肌肉止点移向起点，顺着血液回流心脏的方向，避免把血液向外推。
lock: 按摩压力：从止点向起点。
refs: Manicuring - Massage Principles

why: Proteins supply building material for muscles, blood, and new cells. The body also uses them to repair damaged tissue.
proteins（蛋白质）为肌肉、血液和新细胞提供构建材料，身体也用它修复受损组织。
lock: protein = build and repair body tissue.
蛋白质 = 构建并修复身体组织。
refs: General Anatomy - Nutrition and Proteins

why: Carbohydrates are the body's main quick energy source. Cells break them down to power movement, heat, and normal body functions.
carbohydrates（碳水化合物）是身体主要的快速能量来源。细胞分解它们，为活动、产热和正常功能供能。
lock: 碳水化合物 = 主要供能营养素。
refs: General Anatomy - Nutrition and Carbohydrates

why: Glands take materials from the blood and change them into useful products such as hormones, sweat, oil, or digestive fluids.
glands（腺体）从血液取得材料，并把它们转化为激素、汗液、油脂或消化液等有用物质。
lock: glands make and release body substances.
腺体制造并释放身体物质。
refs: General Anatomy - Glands

why: The pineal gland releases melatonin, a hormone that helps control the sleep-wake cycle. Darkness normally increases its release.
pineal gland（松果体）释放 melatonin（褪黑素），帮助控制睡眠与清醒周期；黑暗通常会增加释放。
lock: pineal gland = melatonin and sleep timing.
松果体 = 褪黑素和睡眠节律。
refs: General Anatomy - Endocrine Glands

why: Protoplasm is the living material inside a cell, including its fluid and working structures. Cell activities take place within it.
protoplasm（原生质）是细胞内的活性物质，包括液体和工作结构；细胞活动在其中进行。
lock: protoplasm = living material of a cell.
protoplasm = 细胞内的活性物质。
refs: General Anatomy - Cells

why: Myology is the study of muscles, including their structure and movement. Osteology is the study of bones.
myology（肌肉学）研究肌肉的结构和动作；osteology（骨学）研究骨。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscular System

why: Minerals give bone its hardness and strength. About two-thirds of bone material is mineral, while the remaining part adds some flexibility.
矿物质让骨坚硬有强度。骨材料约三分之二是矿物质，其余部分提供一定韧性。
lock: 骨 = 约三分之二为矿物质。
refs: General Anatomy - Skeletal System

why: The serratus anterior is a chest muscle that moves the shoulder blade. It is not located in the foot.
serratus anterior（前锯肌）是胸部肌肉，负责移动肩胛骨，并不位于足部。
lock: 前锯肌 = 胸部，不是足部。
refs: General Anatomy - Muscles of the Trunk

notes: All candidates remain unreviewed. Three anatomically vague or subjective items were quarantined.
